items.text: Hi All,
Today we have released a special Steam-only patch that addresses the most common crash reported on Linux.
However, please note that Linux is not a supported system, and in general we might not be able to investigate Linux-specific issues.
All the best and keep those colonists safe.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/59e8bcf4eb8bc9588a9c10df655da2e1259412ee.png"]
Hello Commander,

Our first patch since Feeding the Future is here! We’ve improved how grids handle shortages, reduced Small Farm maintenance costs, and made it easier for Colonists to change trains at Large Stations. The update also includes several more bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements.

Changed the behavior of grids when there is not enough supply to cover the demand. Instead of turning the whole grid off, buildings will be disabled in stages depending on their priority - first, all low priority buildings will shut down; if there is still not enough resource to cover the remaining buildings, the medium priority ones will shut down; finally, if there is still not enough for the remaining buildings, everything will shut down
Reduced the maintenance cost of the Small Farm
Small Farms are now affected by the same things that affect the conventional Farms
The Mineral Treatments upgrade is now available for Hospitals. It still does not apply to the Medical Center spire
Buildings
Fixed an issue where refabbing a building destroyed the resources stored inside it
Fixed an issue where Faction Likes/Dislikes related to shifts were triggered for buildings with automated shifts
Fixed an issue where extractors that were turned off and back on could immediately put surrounding buildings into needing maintenance
Fixed an issue with doubled icons for selected recipe in the Replicator spire
Fixed an issue where a wrong warning message was displayed for Open Farms during Toxic Rains
Fixed an issue where Trains would get deleted when demolishing their Train Station; they are now returned as prefabs
Fixed an issue where destroyed Universal Tunnels became useable again by saving and reloading the savegame
Passage entry points can now be built on Capital City edge hexes
Indoor and outdoor vacant work slots are now listed separately in Domes' info panels
Buildings that can be constructed only once, such as Wonders, no longer show the "for all" control hints for priority, upgrades, etc.
Only one Panoramic Restaurant can now be placed in Diamond Domes in order to avoid severe overlapping
The Hanging Gardens now properly receive a bonus from the Exotic Mineral Structures upgrade
The Curetato can now be grown in the Small Farm
Domes' Oxygen consumption is now removed after the Domes are actually opened, not when the Breathable Atmosphere terraforming threshold is reached
Added a better breakdown of all Dome stat modifiers in the 'Services' rollover of the Dome
Space Elevator UI is broken when opened from the Underground
Colonists
Fixed an issue where Colonists would not take Sanity damage when working in out-Dome buildings
Fixed an issue where Colonists would move to work in turned off Domes. Turning off a Dome will now fire workers from the affected workplaces
Fixed an issue where Colonists would stay for a full visit in a service building after it had switched to an inactive shift; they now properly leave the building and try to visit another time
Made some improvements to Colonists' migration logic. Colonists can now change Trains at Large Stations in order to reach their destination
Children are no longer taken for expeditions that require Colonists
The effect of Heavy Workload on a building's Performance now scales with the number of workers, relative to the overall work slots
Research and Techs
Fixed an issue preventing the 'The Boundaries of Knowledge' achievement from being unlocked
Fixed the rollover of the 'Mysteries' entry in the Research UI when it's unlocked through a non-main mystery

When the 'No Politics' game rule is active, the Independence Tech cluster is hidden. The Human Alteration cluster remains, as it can be unlocked through other means (events, mysteries, commander profiles)
Politics

Fixed an issue preventing the 'Political Animal' achievement from being unlocked. Laws hidden due to prerequisites, as well as such that cannot be active at the same time as others now don't count for the achievement
Fixed an issue where enacting or revoking a law would make the Politics screen jump back to the top. The screen now stays on the selected policy
Faction tasks no longer target specific Domes and can be fulfilled for any Dome
Building Codes' now applies its maintenance modifier to prefab-built buildings too
Resource Subsidies' now grants a discount instead of a free resource, and its penalty was reduced
Double Rations' now grants Morale instead of Comfort
Clarified the description of 'Right to Rest' - it now properly mentions that residences restore Colonist Sanity
Added voting prediction to Laws which are currently being prepared
Added a text clarifying that the selected Law is being prepare
Rockets, Shuttles, Rovers, Drones
Fixed an issue where certain Rockets would not get fully refuelled
Fixed an issue where a Trade Rocket could get stuck due to offers being generated for an invalid Trade Pad
Fixed a case where a Rocket could become unselectable with the cursor when its liftoff timer was interrupted
Fixed an issue where Shuttles wouldn't load Elevators with custom resource settings
Fixed more instances of interrupted Drones that drop resources in inaccessible places
Resources no longer pile up in the middle of the outside ranches
Rockets marked for salvaging can no longer pick a destination, have their cargo edited or appear as available in the Planetary View
Japan's Wasp Drones will no longer jump over or fly through tall buildings and obstacles, but will rather go around them
Resupply
Fixed a case where Traits would get clipped in the passenger filters
Fixed an issue breaking the UI when using the Space Elevator from the Resupply menu while in the Underground or on Asteroids
Added a control for adding/removing a 100 units of a resource in the automated payload UI
The 'Mars' section now lists available resources on both the surface and in the Underground
Fixed an issue that allowed ordering of Food through the Space Elevator when the 'Hunger' game rule is active
Notifications
Fixed an issue where the map wouldn't be changed when selecting a Water Shortage notification
Fixed an issue where the 'Power Shortage' notification would not be displayed after changing maps
Fixed an issue where the 'Power Shortage' notification wouldn't cycle through all of its contents
Fixed an issue where repaired rovers were not removed from the 'Rover damaged' (Logistical Problem) notification
Fixed an issue where salvaged rovers were not removed from the 'Rover damaged' (Logistical Problem) notification
Fixed an issue where rovers were not removed from the 'Heavy drone workload' (Logistical Problem) notification after recalling all Drones
Fixed an issue preventing the cycling of Colonists with controller in notifications
Domes in the 'Missed Meals' notification now display an indication if they are on another map
Realigned the Tech icons in Tech-related notifications
Command Center
Added 'Pack/Unpack Drones' buttons for Rockets in the Transportation menu
Colonist stat values below 30 are now shown in red in the Domes menu
General UI, Controls, Texts
Basics tutorial: Fixed an issue that prevented the opening of the Infrastructure tab in the build menu, blocking the progress of the tutorial
Improved the readability of rollovers displayed over other texts and UI elements
The 'Last Sol' statistics for service and other buildings now means the last three shifts, not the previous calendar day
Added appropriate Lake images in the Encyclopedia (previously all Lakes used the image of the Huge Lake)
Improved the Delicacies encyclopedia entry by adding more visuals and emphasis
Clarified the Agronomist's crop growth bonus - it targets only Farms and Small Farms
Fixed an issue where the WASD keys would not pan the camera when the secondary arrow key bindings were changed

Added back the "Toggle Resource Icons" key binding. In order to avoid accidental presses and confusion, there is no default key assigned to it; players who wish to use it can set their preferred key in the options
Added new loading screens
Added an animation behind the autosave text
Fixed an issue where buildings would remain clogged after a dust storm event
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/dcc5bc0cc343d2415892bae053f257fb9b6e47bb.png"]
The legacy research system was replaced with a new tech tree.
Research now accumulates toward generating Tech Points.
Tech Points are used to instantly unlock Technologies.
All Technologies cost 1 Tech Point.
Each new Tech Point requires more Research than the last, creating implicit long-term scaling.
Technologies are placed on a spatial, hex-based research grid.
Tech Points can be spent only on adjacent Technologies to already researched nodes.
Wonder Technologies sit far from the origin and require sustained, focused commitment.
Breakthrough Technologies and Mystery/Story Technologies are discovered separately and are not bound to the main research grid.
Initiatives are additional entry points to different sections of the board that you can uplock by completing certain goals.
Anomalies and exploration can unlock off-path Technologies within a capped radius of current progress.
Added ~50 new Technologies.
Added a Search function.

Replaced the old research queue with a new Wishlist. Wishlisted Technologies will be auto-researched when the needed Tech Points and connections become available. The amount of wishlisted Technologies is not capped, but they cannot be freely rearranged in the queue - there are controls to remove Technologies from the Wishlist, to move a selected Technology to the top of the Wishlist, and to clear the whole Wishlist.

Exchange Technology with Rival Colonies is now Exchange Research and works by offering a Technology that the player has unlocked and the Rival hasn't. In exchange, the Rival provides Research. The amount of Research received in this exchange is based on the Rival’s Research per Sol.
Unlocking all the available technologies is possible but extremely hard.
Find out more about Research redesign and the design intent behind it in the "Lab Leaks" Dev Diary.
The legacy Services system that relied on visits was replaced with a new system with an aggregated approach.

The Stats (Health, Sanity, Comfort, Morale) of all Colonists in a Dome are now affected by the availability of Service buildings in that Dome, without the need for Colonists to actually visit the buildings in order to receive their effects. The aggregated bonuses from all available Services are applied to each Colonist every Sol.
The impact on Colonist Stats scales with the building’s Performance.

Each Service building has a Service Type and a Service Capacity. Buildings of the same Type (for example, the Spacebar and the Small Spacebar) are combined into a single pool that affects the entire Dome.
Some Service Types are age-specific - Playgrounds provide their bonuses only to children, and Spacebars are only for adults.
When a Service Type has less Capacity than the Dome population, the Stat gain is reduced proportionally.
The Capacity scales with the number of open workshifts.
Any spare Capacity can be used by Colonists in connected Domes with no penalty.

Comfort and Morale now have a current value and a Target value for each Colonist. Service buildings and other modifiers affect the Target rather than the Stat itself, and at each rest the Colonist’s actual stat moves gradually toward the Target.
Working in most workplaces now drains some of the workers' Stats every day. The actual impacted Stats depend on the type of building.
Visits still trigger resource consumption, attendance counters used by laws, and per-visit bonuses.
Workshift changes don't interrupt visits unless the building is left with no active shifts or is outright turned off, in which case the visitors are politely invited to leave.
The new Passage Hub building unlocks more opportunities to create interconnected Domes.
Want to learn more about the Service system overhaul? You can read the “Being of Service” Dev Diary.
The Food resource (and the Delicacies resources in the Feeding the Future DLC) now has a Decay effect. At the end of each Sol, 4% of stockpiled Food will disappear.
Colonists
Colonists now have a Natural Disposition value for Comfort, set at the 20-40 range to introduce some variation in their Stats.
The Hippie Trait now receives a flat +10 Comfort with Parks instead of a 2× multiplier.
The Earthsick status is now applied when below the threshold of 30 Comfort rather than exactly at it.
Founders can no longer get Earthsick.
Removed the Tourist-exclusive Satisfaction Stat. Tourists now rate their experience on Comfort and Morale.
Overstaying Tourists now receive a penalty of −10 Morale per Sol.
Resource availability
Rebalanced the Surface Metals deposits.
Meteors yield less Metals but can now drop Rare Metals and Exotic Minerals.
Buildings construction and maintenance
Raised the building costs in Concrete and Metals.
Slightly increased Concrete maintenance costs.
Buildings
The Space Elevator now operates only in an automated mode and can export all available resources similar to Rockets. It no longer imports non-resource cargo (prefabs). It now travels every 12h.
Naturalist Habitats’ effects on their residents were increased to +40 Comfort, +10 Health, +10 Sanity.
Fungal Farms can no longer be built on the Martian surface.
The Capital City now has a larger workplace radius around it.
The Mohole Mine and The Excavator can now be constructed in the Underground.
Comfort sources values have been broadly rebalanced
Amphitheater +10 (was +20)
Temple +30 (was +40)
Geoscape Dome +20 (was +25)
Martian Festivals +5
Hanging Gardens no longer applies its bonus to Residences but rather gives a +30 Comfort to adult Colonists and now counts as a Decoration for the Ecologist.
Supply grids (Power, Water and Oxygen) now shut down all consumers on an unbalanceable shortage rather than turning off some individual buildings.
Landscaping
All landscaping requires an RC Dozer and can no longer be performed by Drones.
Landscaping times went up ~15%.
"Change Surface" got 50% faster.
Technologies
“Explorer AI” now gives +30% Research per Research-granting Anomaly scanned instead of a flat per-Sol amount.
“Martian Patents” now provides Funding per Sol, increasing with each Tech Point spent, rather than a flat one-time gain.
“Martian Copyrights” now provides 1000 M (was 2000 M).
“Martian Festivals” effect reduced to +5 Comfort (was +10).
Removed “Advanced Mineral Composites”,“Self-Sufficient Lighting” and “Decommission Protocol” (salvage is now available from the start).
Laws
New Law - “Onboarding Program” with a tiered option to spend Funding for the chance of arriving Colonists to develop a Trait.
Removed the “Birth Restrictions” Law.
Replaced “Outsourcing” and “Additional Sponsor Research" with “Research Outsourcing” which provides tiered Research-for-Funding options.
“Sensor Tower” Law effects nerfed to -20% Rocket travel time and +10% Research (from −30%/+30%), and now requires a working tower.
“Resource Subsidy” Law now only affects Earth/Mars/Asteroid travel, not planetary anomalies.
“Black Market” prices are now lower overall and shown per-unit.
Sponsors
Doubled Japan's deep-scan bonus so a direct deep scan matches scanning in two steps.
Church of the New Ark's Hydroponic Farm drawback is now a flat −30 instead of −50%.
Reworked Tutorials
New events
Fixed an issue with the “Growth Stimulators” Tech causing plants to grow 2× slower instead of +50% faster.
Open Farm now shows the building’s total expected production when choosing a crop. Previously it was showing the production per hex.
Fixed some cases in which Tourists were unable to depart - they can now use Shuttles to reach a Rocket.
Fixed an issue where the RC Constructor couldn’t build several buildings.
Fixed a case where Drones building an Elevator would path to spots on another map.
Fixed an issue where the Ancient Artifact disappeared when near the edge of the screen.
Fixed an issue where in some cases Colonists were dying from Hypothermia while on an Expedition.
Fixed an issue where the “Extra Applicants” Law would grant Applicants for Milestones completed by a Rival Colony.

Colonies with Paradox as Sponsor are no longer left without a Shuttle Hub after declaring Independence. These colonies fallback to the default Shuttle Hub. You can regain access to the sponsor-specific buildings after Independence.
Fixed a case in which Dust Storms were still happening despite 100% Atmosphere.
Fixed a case where Shuttles would continue to fly despite there being a Dust Storm.
Destroyed Shuttles now drop their carried resources as stockpiles instead of deleting them.

Fixed cases in which Self-sufficient Domes could be constructed with missing life support buildings. If any of the components are not available as prefabs or researched, the text in the build menu will display the reason.
Fixed cases in which building a Train Station over an existing Track deleted the Track elements next to it.
Fixed a case in which the Construction Nanites Breakthrough would cause Cables to be built incorrectly in segments.
Fixed an issue where landscaping with nanites would not yield Waste Rock.
Fixed an issue where residences in the Underground were not counted as available when ordering a Passenger Rocket.
Dust Devils no longer affect Colonists inside Passages (unless the Domes are opened).
Dust Storm effects now start only on maps that actually have them.
New Rocket workflow

notes.title: Added several new buttons in Rockets’ info panels

items.text: "Select destination" - pick from all the available destinations without opening the Planetary View separately;
"Accept fuel" - enable or disable the refueling of the Rocket;
"Carry return trip fuel" - enable or disable the loading of additional return trip fuel when the Rocket's destination is an Asteroid;

"Wait for manual launch" - enable or disable automatic take-off once loading/unloading is completed and there are no other problems with the Rocket (only applicable for manual mode when the destination is Earth).

When the destination is set to Earth and the Rocket is in manual mode, an “Exports” section appears in its info panel, allowing the on/off toggling of all exportable resources (Rare Metals and Exotoc Minerals, plus Fuel when playing with Oligarch). The export amount cannot be tweaked in manual mode - the Rocket will try to load as much as possible from the allowed resources. If you’d like to be more precise with the amounts you export, use automated mode - there are no changes there.
Rockets arriving to Mars from Earth will set their destination to Earth automatically.
Rockets now have a 3-second grace period just before departing. During that time, you can change requests, cancel the flight or perform any other actions.
Opening Planetary View, picking a destination and choosing a Rocket for it works as before - there are no changes there.
Added the buttons for packing and unpacking of Drones to the info panels of Rockets.
General UI
The build menu now better highlights the availability of prefabs and the locked/unlocked state of buildings.
The first Rocket landing shows deposits in range.
Rearranged some build menu items.
Reordered the list of Commander Profiles - recommended first, then by challenge rating.
Added a low-Comfort warning in the Colonist info panel.
Colonist stat breakdown now lists named modifiers separately (e.g. beauty deposits show as "Vista" under Comfort).
Selecting a Tech in the "New Tech Unlocked" notification opens the Research screen focused on that tech.

Some fullscreen UIs now have a rollover text when hovering the cursor over their title. It's indicated by an “i” icon on the right side of the title. The corresponding controller support was also added for displaying these hints while holding down a button.
Train Stations now connect to Domes that have at least one entrance inside the Station’s work radius to make the answer to the “is this Dome serviced by this Station” question more intuitive.
Added an “Expected Funding” row in the Rocket’s infopanel if the destination is set to Earth.
Added rollover tooltips for Milestones.
“Global Support” breakthrough - buildings that are unlocked are shown in a notification.
Removed the “Increase approval by” section from the faction’s rollover as that is now explained in the “Approves of/Disapproves of” sections.
The resource bar now shows the actual consumption for the current grid, displays the single most-prominent grid on-screen (refreshed once per second), and hides Seeds when unavailable.
Pipe hexes are visible during placement of all buildings.
Added a warning when a construction will block the pipe connection hex of another building.
Workplace infopanel now shows Performance as a percentage.
Water and Oxygen resources now have separate rollovers in the Resource Bar.
The Funding rollover now provides additional information on how Funding is gained and spent.
Planetary expeditions now prefer Unemployed Colonists, as employed expedition-goers keep their job slots which stops buildings from working.
Resources from destroyed buildings now fit into a small number of taller piles instead of a lot of normal-sized piles.
You can now buy more than 20 Drones with resupply Rockets from Earth. Rockets still can control only 20, so if the excess Drones can’t find another controller nearby, they will get orphaned.
Added a toggle option for Electronics storage in the info panel of the Recon Center.
The RC Dozer now clears Cave-ins when in automated mode.
The RC Dozer now looks for Waste Rock needed for landscaping projects in a larger radius instead of just waiting.
The RC Dozer will no longer dump Waste Rock on the ground, unless it’s full and it needs to continue working on a project. If there is a Dumping Site nearby, it will unload the Waste Rock there.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/44530ec2beb35a4e22528addc975c5fca1af0d0b.jpg"]Hello everyone,

After the release of Surviving Mars: Relaunched, we made a choice to focus on the base game first — listening to your feedback and delivering a series of updates to make sure the foundation was as strong as possible. Lots of patches have happened (and you can read a summary of all of them here), with the latest one being 1.0.7, which included major changes.

That focus has meant shifting our attention to post-launch content a little later than originally planned. As a result, after many discussions, we are shifting the Feeding the Future content pack release to Q3 instead of Q2, which will let us stay focused on development and make sure that we provide a good experience for you. It was a hard decision to make, but we're confident it was the right call — and now we're fully focused on making Feeding the Future something you'll truly love.
To make sure you are in the loop and know what’s happening, we have prepared a Dev Diary with a sneak peek of what is to come, and you can read it below!

However, we also want to make sure that you will have a great time playing both the base game and our upcoming DLC, and for that, we want to let you shape the content with us - with the help of the Closed Beta program. If you want to help us get some feedback on the upcoming content, feel free to sign up, and you may become one of the participants!
JOIN THE BETA

Additionally, we want to assure you that we will continue working on the free patches to keep improving your experience and quality of life in the game. All the feedback you provide is highly appreciated and makes Surviving Mars: Relaunched better.

notes.title: Is This Even the Same Game?

items.text: The changes planned for the free update and the “Feeding the Future” DLC are substantial, to put it mildly. There are drastic changes to research, services, and needs.
You will hear more about the changes to Food in a future dev diary.
The game has outgrown the old research system. We are building a larger system that supports more technologies and new choices. Expect a large number of new research techs as well.

The new system supports different research builds, and you can access some advanced technologies relatively early if you pursue them. To balance this, you will need to spend tech points, which are awarded when you reach ever-increasing research point thresholds. Getting all of the technologies is very expensive. Research is now about deciding which technologies you want to get first, and which ones to give up entirely in this playthrough.

We weren’t satisfied with the service system or the amount of information you needed to track to keep your colonists happy. We have shifted to a different system in which services directly affect colonists’ stats.

The new system does not rely on visits. Each service type counts the number of colonists serviced, then averages the building effect across the entire population. As a result, both the quality of the service and the quantity (accessibility) are important.
For example, Parks improve colonists’ Sanity and Comfort. Gyms improve their Health and Comfort. Some buildings, like the Spacebar, reduce a colonist’s Sanity while greatly increasing their Comfort.
Different professions also affect which stats are lost: people working in extractors will lose Health every day, while colonists in research buildings will lose Sanity.
Colonists can use services in Domes directly connected to their own, but only if those services have excess capacity after colonists in that Dome have been serviced.
This change has significantly affected my gameplay, as I am more strategic about what I put into Domes, and the game feels new and unknown again.

notes.title: Again, here is a teaser for you

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/5c80ebc530d0d817abb01cf71cdbac3957f543cb.png"]

The changes to food come mostly from the DLC. In addition to the basic food, you will be able to produce Food Ingredients that flavor the food in the food service buildings. They are an optional way for your food to also give you stat bonuses to Health, Comfort, and Morale. Some of the Food Ingredients are produced directly as crops, some are a by-product of a crop (or an animal breed), and some can only be received from processing in a new building.
Having a lot of Food Ingredients will allow you to stack up quite hefty bonuses to your stats but will require a lot of production of these resources.
Additionally, expect new Food Service buildings, laws, and techs.

The changes in Politics feel much more subtle by comparison, but they are still impactful. You will now be able to vote on laws whenever you want, but you will still need to wait for new laws to be prepared. This will allow you to change your political system quickly while still slowly exploring its laws.
Big changes are coming to the game, and I hope you are ready for them. We are just getting started.
Keep your colonists safe and your colonies growing until you hear from us again!
The Haemimont Team

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/8727b25678c86dd74cb8a5b6bf33dadcd889742c.png"]

As outlined in Haemimont Diaries #1, we’re introducing a major rework of the Rockets by converting the existing ones to universal Rockets that can be sent to all destinations, Asteroids included. Following your feedback and reactions to this announcement, we decided against removing the Asteroid Lander – it will remain available for use. Read all the details below.

When ordering a Cargo Rocket from the Resupply menu, you are now taken through a Select Destination screen where you choose where to send the Rocket – to Mars or to an Asteroid (if available). Rocket cargo is then displayed according to the destination.

Asteroid Landers bought from Earth will still have a default destination Mars and you’ll be able to manage them once they arrive on the Red Planet. As before, they can only be used to travel between Mars and Asteroids. Asteroid Landers require less Fuel than regular Rockets and have increased cargo space.
Rockets on Mars will no longer set Earth as their default destination and will not be refueled if no destination is set.

Going through the new “Destination” button in the Rocket’s info panel will open the Planetary View and allow you to choose where to send the Rocket – we’ve added Earth here too! The flow for expeditions and Asteroids works exactly as before, but if you’re sending a Rocket back to Earth, you’ll be taken through a payload screen where you can set the amount of exports. On that note, you’ll now be able to export Exotic Minerals in addition to Rare Metals!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/68e15cdf5601df6b009579640af92b4443787d77.png"]

To facilitate fast return to Earth without going through the Planetary View and exports setup, the new “Back to Earth” button will automatically start preparing the Rocket for its return trip, not loading any exports.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/40a2103f0100469210f316cbed6f6d2007e0e0f5.png"]

In order to improve the flow of resupply and exports, we’ve reworked the automated mode to a universal screen where you can manage everything at once depending on the location and destination of the Rocket. Need a steady supply of free Polymers after enacting the Resource Subsidies Law? You can set that up and forget about it. Want to continuously export precious loot to Earth and get some Food resupplies for your Asteroid-dwellers? We’ve got you covered.

In order to avoid long waiting times and keep the auto mode running smoothly, Rockets with a pending payload have a one Sol maximum waiting period for collection of exports, after which they will depart – you can see the countdown in the Rocket’s info panel and in the Payload screen.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/e74115437d9b99e1f7408c531fe3bcc9048a6301.png"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/057aed6db9d3586f2d7dbffc82ed53c2993c38c1.png"]
All changes related to the Rockets will apply to new and existing saves.

Another change that we covered in Haemimont Diaries #1 concerned the expiration of Asteroids and the available resources there. While there’s still more that we want to explore in that direction, we consider the modifications in 1.0.7 a significant improvement over 1.0.6. Here is a rundown of the changes.

Asteroids are no longer time-limited – they will be tracked permanently until manually abandoned. This means that the Capture Asteroid Breakthrough and the Asteroid Catcher building have been retired. To help you navigate this new reality, you’re now able to abandon an Asteroid directly from its icon in the HUD.
We’ve also tweaked the rate at which Asteroids are discovered, so you can expect them to be a bit rarer than before.

A final change here concerns the Gotcha! achievement, which has been changed from catching an Asteroid with the Catcher to having to track two Asteroids at the same time; already unlocked achievements will be maintained.
In saves pre-1.0.7

Already constructed Asteroid Catchers will be preserved as a “monument of our continued progress” (they might make a comeback in the future). All existing and newly-discovered Asteroids will become permanent.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/001b8cf21aeb5d1c478a33856c33d87109ed1c40.png"]
In saves pre-1.0.7
The new “slot” system and upgrades will not apply and all existing Recon Centers will keep functioning as before. New ones will not be available for construction.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/2a06488017bcc211f333ad661efb5feee37eaa56.png"]

Another change concerning buildings is that the Micro-G Auto Extractor and the Micro-G Mining Station are now split into three variants for each specific resource – Metals, Rare Metals or Exotic Minerals, aiming to give you more control over the resources that you want to extract.
In saves pre-1.0.7
The old buildings will keep being functional, but not available for construction – the three new variants will be available instead.

The Space Miner Commander Profile has been updated in accordance with all changes – you will still receive bonus Techs and prefabs and will also start with a discovered Asteroid, ready to be conquered.

As previously mentioned, we’ve further tweaked the buildable space on Asteroids and rebalanced the available resources. You can expect some Asteroids to have more resources scattered on their surface, while others will offer a treasure trove of underground deposits. We hope that these balance changes, along with everything else, will make Asteroids more exciting for visiting and more worth exploiting.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/c75774d82a9ba84c8affe0841dbe2c42f40083c0.png"]

One highly requested feature since the introduction of the Passages has been the ability to attach them to the rims of Domes instead of taking from the buildable hexes inside. In 1.0.7, you can now officially do that! Passages can be placed on most of the Domes’ perimeter hexes, with some exceptions where entrances, pipe connectors or specific curves prevent this. The option to place them in hexes inside the Domes is also maintained, so you have more options to connect your Domes as you see fit.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/967dbd1bad48c36accc8ae7da6a7172772da9083.png"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/73b2aeeadc152d8d20b6063c0e1815f8a7c597ad.png"]
Asteroids no longer have an expiration timer. The related Breakthrough – Capture Asteroid – has been removed. The Asteroid Catcher building has been retired.
Players start with the ability to track and visit only 1 Asteroid (1 Asteroid “slot”). The number of “slots” can be increased by the Recon Center building.

The Recon Center is now a unique building (only one can be constructed) that players can upgrade. Each upgrade level provides +1 “slot” for Asteroids that can be tracked and visited. In older saves, the “slot” system will not apply. The other Recon Center mechanics remain the same.
Micro-G Auto Extractors and Micro-G Mining Stations are now split into variants for a specific resource - Metals, Rare Metals or Exotic Minerals. This change will not affect old savegames.
The Space Miner Commander Profile has been modified according to the related changes.
Asteroids now have more buildable space.
Balance changes have been made so some Asteroids have more resources scattered on their surface.
Rockets can now travel to Asteroids. They can also make the journey directly between Earth and an Asteroid.
Automated mode: Implemented an automated flight mode for Rockets traveling between Earth, Mars, and Asteroids, including an auto-depart logic.
Exotic Minerals can now be exported to Earth.
Fixed some cases in which 1 passenger will remain in rocket cargo after returning from a Planetary Anomaly.
Passages can now be attached to the sides of the Domes.
Fixed an issue where Outside Ranches wouldn’t work with "Too far from Domes" error.
Fixed an issue where the in-dome Ranch would not work properly when switching between different animals.
Fixed an issue that would cause Domes using a skin different than the default one to not be correctly damaged by meteors or orbital bombardment.
Fixed an issue where RC Constructors could get confused and not load needed resources or contribute to a construction they were ordered to.
RC Constructors will no longer get stuck when constructing Lakes.
Fixed rare cases where buildings would not be completed or repaired by an RC Constructor.
Fixed an issue where Drones would not work on cave-ins under certain circumstances.
Fixed cases in which an RC Safari was not registering as an available service to Domes when there was a rover in close proximity.
Fixed cases in which Underground Entrances could spawn too close to each other, resulting in Elevators becoming unavailable for placement.
Underground Entrances can no longer be spawned on top ofdust geysers.
Fixed a rare case where rovers could get stuck inside rocks in the Underground.
Fixed cases in which Solar Panels were not properly facing the sun or the Artificial Sun.
The Elevator is now properly disabled during the Elevator Malfunction event.
Drone Hub Extenders now work properly with the Wireless Power Breakthrough.
Fixed an issue where RC Dozers would drop Waste Rock on the ground instead of in nearby Dumping Sites.
Fixed an issue where Drones could get stuck in loops during construction of Domes.
Fixed multiple problems with construction and power of the Bottomless Pit and cases where the Anomaly associated with it would appear in a different cave.
When copied, Universal Storages now properly remember what resources are allowed.
Fixed buildings incorrectly displaying no power in older saves.
Fixed more cases where colonists would get stuck near buildings.
Fixed stuck colorizations during building placement.
Improvements in various building sounds.
Fixed an issue where Colonists would move to live in nonfunctional Domes.
Fixed an issue where Colonists would prefer to work in a neighbouring Dome instead of the one they live in if all other factors were equal.
Fixed an issue where Colonists sent on Expedition would appear as Homeless in the resource bar.
Fixed an issue where incorrect reachability checks prevented Colonists and Tourists from properly boarding Rockets or using Elevators.
Fixed an issue where Colonists were still being employed in buildings with the Service Bots and similar upgrades that remove workers completely.
Fixed cases in which Colonists were interrupted while commuting by Train, causing them to walk large distances and suffocate.
Fixed a freeze related to Tourists exiting an RC Safari that was destroyed.
Fixed a freeze related to using the Follow Camera for a Colonist on a different map.
Fixed cases in which workplaces would not remove non-specialists when there were specialists available to work there or were working with the wrong specialization.
Fixed more cases where many Colonists would be fired at the same time because they were trying to work in a place they cannot reach.
Fixed a rare case in which Tourists could be sent to Earth twice.
Fixed cases in which Colonists would suffocate when moving between different Naturalist Habitats.
Notifications for low Power, Oxygen, or Water storage now trigger when reserves fall below 30 hours of supply (previously 3 days).
Added a building warning for the Open Farms when the Soil Quality requirements of the selected crops are not met.
Implemented construction warnings for Domes to notify players when a Dome is not connected to an underground Elevator, which would prevent Colonists moving in them.
Added a building warning when Lakes do not increase Water because the Liquid Water threshold has not been reached.
“Funding received” notification now includes profits from Black Market exports.
Added UI notifications for stored Trains due to a removed Track/Station or when the Train was marked for stopping.

Fixed an issue where if the player made the Drones invulnerable with the Ancient Artefact and got the AI mystery, this could lead to a situation where immortal Drones could destroy everything in sight.
Fixed an issue where additional Applicants were still being generated after Earth had been quarantined under the Wildfire mystery.
The Power Of Three mystery now looks for a Power Accumulator if a Concrete Extractor is not present, making it less likely to block the unlocking of the S.H.E.P.I.D. research.
Fixed an issue where loading an old savegame could in certain cases crash the game.
Fixed various freezes related to the Underground.
Various performance improvements and hardlock fixes.
Various crash fixes.
Fixed the issue where Sponsor logos added as mods would appear upside down.
Modders can now make any resource exportable to Earth.
The Rockets fuel logic is no longer locked to only the resource “Fuel”. Modders can also now choose a resource that Rockets can use as fuel.

The rocket rework moves all old rocket classes into a new one called UniversalRocketBase and all supply pods in UniversalSupplyPodBase. Now, the FlightPolicyDef presets are responsible for what a rocket could do in a different way based on its arrival location.
The Landscaping Nanites Breakthrough now allows working on landscape projects without Drones, even when the construction site needs to be cleared.
Fixed various cases where Drones would continuously attempt tasks they could not actually complete, such as reaching unreachable piles of Waste Rock.
Fixed a case where Japan’s flying Drones would get stuck in a loop.
Fixed a freeze related to Rockets trying to load Drones.
Added a shortcut that hides all UI – Ctrl+Shift+U.
Ctrl+F1 to report bugs is now listed in the Options under Key Bindings.
Planet Anomalies and Expeditions now display the available Rockets properly.
The names of the completed Special Projects are now shown in the rollover of the Planetary View button.
Fixed the Residential Space launch issue message that claimed that there was no living space when Colonists were sent to Asteroids with available living space.
Fixed some cases in which Underground Entrance markers would appear under the Entrance.
Fixed some cases in which building ranges and highlighted hexes would get stuck.
Sectors are no longer visible in the Underground.
Added a warning in the info panels of Forestation Plants clarifying that they will improve Vegetation while it is less than 40%.
Added a hint on how to set the default building in cases where multiple buildings are listed in the same slot in the build menu.
The construction grid is no longer hidden when constructing on slopes.
The effects of Independence are better explained in the Mission Profile.
Filter controls will no longer appear in Passenger Rockets for groups that currently have no Colonists.
Added a toggle in Photo Mode that controls whether the Domes are opened or closed.
Fixed some cases in which Command Center filters were incorrectly displayed as OFF.
The Command Center now properly displays Train statistics under Graphs.
Fixed a case where constructions did not show an on-cursor message with the reason for restricted placement.

Tracks are now constructed in groups of up to 5 elements, bringing them in line with other infrastructure like Pipes and Cables. Salvaging Track constructions will now cancel only the last element and not the whole Track.
Various fixes related to unsalvageable or unusable Tracks.
Fixed many cases in which Trains would get stuck.
Additional fixes for old saves where Stations could not properly connect to each other.
Fixed a freeze related to looped Stations.
Fixed a case in which Trains could not be constructed.
Fixed some cases in which Drones would not build certain Track segments.
The game will be paused when a controller is disconnected (Steam).
Fixed another instance of lighting breaking after switching maps, leading to a sepia-like effect.
The Terraforming Focus Law can no longer be used when the No Terraforming rule is active.
Rival Colonies will no longer show duplicated Trade Routes for the same resource.
Fixed an issue related to properly handling cases where there is no support for any political Faction.
The Mars Reservation will no longer remove rocks inside it.
Fixed Faction tasks that were incorrect or had wrong prerequisites.
The Ally option for Post-Independence Earth Relations properly reduces import costs.
Soil Quality now properly decreases after landscaping.
Reduced the number of Vistas and Research Sites spawned from the Designed Forestation Breakthrough.
Seeds will now appear in the initial payload screen when the sponsor is Terraforming Initiative.
Fixed cases where workshifts would get stuck after abandoning Asteroids.
Various visual improvements related to particles.
Resource and other terrain icons are not displayed in older saves in normal camera mode - they are only visible in Overview. It is not present in newly-started 1.0.7 games.
Left-clicking while placing a Passage doesn’t create a “check point” for a turn.
In rare cases, rivals may offer to trade 0 of a resource. A fix will follow in the next patch.
There may be isolated issues with Rockets in older saves - we’ve fixed a number of problems, but were not able to cover all possible scenarios and Rocket states in savegames.
We’ve kept fixing issues with stuck particles and other visuals, but there are problems which we are still in the process of isolating and addressing.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/7e21620b7980a86d8cc470eeea6b156ac591cb33.png"]
Hey everyone,

We’re back with Patch 1.0.6, bringing a round of fixes, refinements, and system improvements. This update reworks the Underground Elevator, further integrates the Surface and Underground grids, and smooths out a number of issues affecting Mysteries, Politics, Trains, and Asteroids.
Underground Elevator rework

[p align="justify"]In 1.0.6 we’ve changed how the Underground Elevator functions. The resource transfer UI for the Underground Elevator has been removed. The Elevator now works like a Universal storage that’s available both on the surface and in the underground. And just like a Universal storage you can allow or forbid it from taking specific resources.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/42a55083b8cc120ae9c9b401e6b13fe59ce71ef5.png"]Drones will then be able to use the stored resources both for the surface and the underground maps as needed.
[p align="justify"]We’ve also added new commands that tell the elevator where you want a resource to be used - on the Surface or in the Underground.
[p align="justify"]For example, I can set the Elevator to only take out Waste Rock on the surface and then the drones will feed all that Waste Rock to be used on the surface of Mars.
[p align="justify"]Transport Rovers can overrule this with their Load/Unload resource or Transport Route commands.

[p align="justify"]Colonists will be able to move from the surface to the underground and vice versa to find Domes where they can live and work. If you want to limit certain colonist specializations not to go underground, you can use the Dome filters.

[p align="justify"]Another change in 1.0.6 is that if connected via the Elevator, the Surface and Underground life support and power grids now act as if they are part of the same grid, rather than two separate grids that try to balance each other. This solves multiple issues where either the grid production is doubled or is not transferred at all.

[p align="justify"]Elevators in saves from older versions will work but in some cases might encounter issues with their connected pipes and cables. The solution is to demolish the pipes and cables and rebuild them.
[p align="justify"]In Patch 1.0.6 we introduced a number of changes that aim to make the Underground more accessible and integrated with the rest of the game.

[p align="justify"]There are no longer special domes and players can now build all of the regular domes in the Underground but they will consume 50% more power. This makes the “Underground Dome Construction” tech obsolete so it was removed.
[p align="justify"]The Jumbo Cave mystery objectives and rewards were tweaked to reflect these changes.

[p align="justify"]We’ve split the Mineral Applications tech into 2 new ones - the Advanced Mineral Composites that will increase solar panels power production and Mineral Treatments that will increase health and sanity recovery from Infirmary and Medical post.

[p align="justify"]The Spelunker Commander profile no longer has the Bonus tech: Underground Domes. Instead he has a new effect where Underground domes have a lower power consumption penalty (25% instead of 50%).

notes.title: There are also issues that were fixed including

items.text: The radius in which buildings and units (colonists, drones, rovers, …) will light up the underground has been increased.
The Pipes and Cables in the underground when broken would reveal as much of the surrounding darkness as a building would. They now reveal a much smaller radius.

The Elevator could be used to transport rovers and drones between maps even when it is not working (due to malfunction, lack of power, or being stopped) . Think of this as an emergency mode for the Elevator and no - the drones are not using the stairs.

[p align="justify"]Mysteries have received a lot of attention in 1.0.6. The previous patch fixed some underlying global issues that could break the sequences while in this one we’ve closed many of the things that could cause specific steps in the sequences to not trigger.
[p align="justify"]This solves many of the reported issues with the different mysteries.
[p align="justify"]Unfortunately existing games have the old sequence baked into the savegame.

notes.title: Failed to initialize graphics subsystem Error

items.text: [p align="justify"]We know that some players have been hitting this blanket statement error and not finding it helpful. Take note that even newer GPUs can encounter this if the drivers are outdated. Specifically DirectX12 and Shader Model 6.6 are required. If those are not present the game will encounter this error.
[p align="justify"]To make this more evident we’ve changed the Error message to be more descriptive and let the player know what they could do to resolve this.
[p align="justify"]Asteroids got some nice-to-have changes
[p align="justify"]Waste Rock can once again be transported by Asteroid Landers.
[p align="justify"]Seeds are no longer a viable payload item for the Asteroid Lander. Any loaded seeds in existing games will be unloaded by drones.

[p align="justify"]RC Commanders will now be loaded in the lander rockets together with all drones they are controlling. The manual asteroid lander and resupply UI now shows the total drones in colony/mars not controlled by an RC Commander on the row "Drones".
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where an RC Explorer could be counted twice by the Explorer AI tech if it was sent to an Asteroid.
[p align="justify"]We’ve tackled some of the more common issues as well as implemented some changes that should make Trains more useful
[p align="justify"]Increased the number of colonists a train can carry to 12 (was 8)
[p align="justify"]Players can now build train stations over existing tracks.
[p align="justify"]Fixed several issues that could cause colonists to get stuck (sometimes indefinitely) while waiting for a train at the Train station.
[p align="justify"]Deleting a track will now prefab trains at stations that are still associated with it.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where in some cases track segments would become undemolishable.
[p align="justify"]Resolved more instances of tracks and stations not connecting properly.
[p align="justify"]We’ve invested the time to resolve some visual issues.
[p align="justify"]The infamous issue where the lighting would rapidly switch between day and night is now resolved.
[p align="justify"]Fixed the issue of lighting being darker than usual shortly after switching from the Underground to the surface map.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue with smoke and other particles remaining on the map after their source is gone.
[p align="justify"]Landing pads are no longer camouflaged during cold waves.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where a Meteor impact prediction marker would be stuck on the map.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where a red flashing light would linger on some drones.
[p align="justify"]Shrouded Wind Turbines now correctly receive the boosts to productivity from Frictionless Composite breakthrough, Terraforming and storybits. This will apply to older savegames.

[p align="justify"]Tunnels and Train tunnels are now replaced by a single Universal tunnel building that can work as both. They can transport colonists, trains and connect life support and electrical grids. The old buildings will appear in savegames from previous versions but won’t be buildable from this patch on.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/9d1b1eae7081188495fb3c57e955a78e25163438.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/f69129b0af74e29e85b348c7ea9164b96e780eab.png"]
Fixed an issue where in certain cases colonists would not change home domes when forced through Dome filters.
Fixed an issue where refabing Naturalists Habitats could break the colonists pathing logic making them unable to find their way to a dome and dying.
Fixed an issue where Project Phoenix could generate colonists with incompatible traits (e.g. Martianborn + Founder).
Children-only and Senior-only living spaces are no longer counted in the Resource bar nor used for the “Births are forbidden when full” calculation.
Fixed cases where an inordinate amount of Tourists were reported as leaving on rockets
Fixed an exploit where funding from departing tourists would trigger upon boarding the rocket. It now triggers when the rocket reaches Earth.
Clarified the status of Colonists that committed suicide due to an event that can override the Religious trait.
[p align="justify"]We’ve made a mix of bugfixes, balance and quality of life changes to the politics system.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where Faction would constantly spam trigger a faction radicalization disaster.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where some players would get the Martian Assembly stuck on “1 hour until next session“.
[p align="justify"]Fixed multiple issues of the Politics or the Laws UI stopping their normal function
[p align="justify"]Added a new notification that highlights when a faction has gained or lost its representation in the Assembly.

[p align="justify"]Detainment and Media Centers no longer have default selected factions upon finishing construction. They start without a target assigned and display a warning for the player to assign one.
[p align="justify"]Added a disabled condition so that the Dictatorship cannot be enacted if there are more than 10% Renegades leading to the law to be auto-repealed later.
[p align="justify"]Limited the amount of Renegades that can be created from the Renegade faction disaster.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where the New Sol faction could dislike you not having services even if you don’t have any colonists yet.
[p align="justify"]Voting Probability rollover with likes/dislikes by faction will now show only factions which have at least one seat in the assembly.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where the law's rollover would give the opinion of factions with no seats in the Assembly.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where in certain cases the overview mode would look blacked out.
[p align="justify"]Restored the keybinding shortcuts for buildings.
[p align="justify"]The Autosave and Quicksave no longer deselect building placement.
[p align="justify"]Asteroid lander payload UI now has the Press and Hold command active.
[p align="justify"]Resources in all Asteroid Lander payload UIs can be increased/decreased by holding the mouse key or a button on the controller
[p align="justify"]Added protection for accidental doubleclick to the build menu and pin items (like ordering rockets to land on the ground below the pin).

[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where the Low Storage warning would display incorrect calculations for remaining time until something runs out. The Notifications and Resource bar rollover no longer have discrepancies.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where some players would get a negative number of colonists (eg. “-5 Earthborn”) in the infopanel rollover.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where some resources were displayed as being negative (e.g. -1 Machine parts) in the resource transfer UIs.
[p align="justify"]Residential buildings now have their Comfort quality listed in the Build menu.
[p align="justify"]Getting funds from Black Market is now displayed in the Funding notification.
[p align="justify"]The Resource Bar no longer shows partial grids that are made up only of Cables/Pipes or have only consumers.
[p align="justify"]Changed the wording of the Trade route choice dialogs to add clarity.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where in certain cases "No sector set for scanning" warning could be missing on the Surface Map but present in the Underground.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where Some Earthsick Colonists are displayed as "Deported" in the Rocket's info panel.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where the Naturalists Habitats would refer to their food consumption as “Comfort food”. Food is essential and is not related to the Comfort level.
[p align="justify"]Added a disabled state for the “Clear Rubble” button for before the player researches the tech that unlocks it.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where it was possible for selector UIs (like the ones for selecting crops in farms) to get stuck and remain on the screen.
[p align="justify"]The Pipe Leak and Cable Fault infopanels now show the repair costs.
[p align="justify"]The “Milestone achieved” notification will now show which Milestone it's referring to.
[p align="justify"]The RC Commander rollover in the Resupply UI now shows how many free drones it comes with the rover.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where some of the hexes used to display ranges for buildings would be missing.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where effect radius visualization would persist even after unselecting the object it was related to.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where in some cases Colonists weren’t wearing the correct uniforms for their specialization.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue with Rare Metals not being displayed in rockets returning from Planetary missions.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue in which the Dumping sites could show there was stored waste rock when in reality the amount was 0.
[p align="justify"]Drones no longer fill Dumping sites by order of their construction. They will now choose the closest one.
[p align="justify"]Reduced the collision boxes of the Low-G Lab and MDS Laser buildings so they don’t cause situations where colonists could get stuck between them and die.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where drones would not conduct maintenance on buildings in specific cases.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where in some cases fully automated Factories would turn themselves off and display the “Not enough workers” warning”.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where a Landing Pad would become unusable and unsalvageable if a rocket was sent to a Planetary anomaly expedition and got destroyed.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where MDS Lasers would not work as expected.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where colonists were starving in Naturalist Habitats that were filled with food.
[p align="justify"]Naturalist Habitats now have On/Off and Priority controls like other buildings.
[p align="justify"]Made the Core Heat Convector impossible to freeze.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where the Biome Engineering tech would not grant increased Comfort from Farms.
[p align="justify"]Extractors can exploit shallow deposits even if they overlap with a deep deposit and the required tech for it is not researched yet.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where some tall Spires could appear cut short.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where the Truly Independent Achievement could be unlocked by completing the Sponsor goals instead of the Post-Independence ones.
[p align="justify"]Landing Supply pods no longer count towards the “You can't take the Sky from Me!” achievement.
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where sending an expedition while on the Underground map wouldn’t acknowledge that you have a rocket available on the surface.
[p align="justify"]Fixed a potential exploit where player could use an RC Transporter to overload a rocket with Rare Metals

[p align="justify"]New Option for Controllers is added in the Controls section - “Focus info panel on selection”. (Disabled by default. When enabled, selecting an object will automatically select the first interactable element in the info panel (as if the D-pad right is pressed).)
[p align="justify"]Fixed an issue where in certain situations the mouse cursor could steal the focus from the controller.
[p align="justify"]Add new LT shortcuts for the Politics and Planetary View.
[p align="justify"]LT + A - open the Politics.
[p align="justify"]LT + B - open the Planetary View.
In the Mission Sponsor mod item we’ve added the ability to add a Sponsor Logo directly without the need of making a Decal mod item.
Introduced the Scenarios mod item that will grant modders the ability to create events.
Import mod item can now properly reloads FBX if it’s loaded in the importer and placed in the mod folder
Alongside this major update, a small server side patch will be coming later today to address a few additional fixes and will download automatically once it becomes available.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/22c627a854e567ef853bf4d161bea904b84d86e0.png"]
Hello Commander,

We’re back with another update, addressing some of the most common issues and quality-of-life improvements you’ve been reporting. This patch includes fixes for crashes and softlocks, improvements to Asteroids and Landers, adjustments to trains and underground systems, and a number balance changes. We’ve also added a new structure, the Shrouded Wind Turbine.🍃 Check it out and let us know what you think!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/f59b48c677a817cce824e032699d6c474747f4c9.png"]
If you see a bug or want to give us direct feedback, press Ctrl+F1 on your PC while in-game to open the bug reporter or go to our Forum.
Implemented a new building - Shrouded Wind Turbine - a large turbine that can be rotated.
Fixed an issue where the Mystery progress could be lost, blocking further progression. This fix applies only to new games; existing savegames may still be affected.
Fixed an issue where colonists could get stuck in the universal depot and die from suffocation.
Quality of Life
Players can now move the Martian Assembly. This happens via a button in the building’s infopanel.
Underground entrances are now visible on the map at game start.
Added shortcuts for +5 and Max Quantity in all resource transfer UIs.
Increased the Dumping Sites’ Waste Rock capacity by a factor of 4. In existing savegames this will also increase the amount of Waste Rock already stored by the same factor.
Dumping Sites now display the max stored amount in their description.
Crashes and Softlocks
Fixed a softlock on the Research screen.
Fixed several common causes of crashes.
Trains
Fixed an issue where train tracks would not transfer power if built in a specific order.
Fixed an issue where in some cases trains would transport some resources endlessly and not load others.
Trains can now be added to Pins.
Asteroids
Reduced the number of deposits spawned on Asteroids but greatly increased the quantity of resources in each deposit.
Fixed an issue where the Asteroid Lander would keep its landing site reserved even after canceling the auto mode.
Further tweaks to Asteroid maps generation to provide more landing spots in some cases. This will not affect existing Asteroid maps.
Landers can now "blow away" debris when landing so small objects like rocks will not hinder the landing site.
Politics
Fixed an issue where the rightmost laws were not being shown in the Laws UI.
Fixed an issue where in some cases the Factory Automation law was not working.

A new notification has been added when the Governing Assembly law is active (the Assembly proposes and votes on laws automatically unless the player overrides it with another choice). At the start of the session it shows what the Assembly plans to do when the session closes.
A new notification has been added when the Governing Assembly law is active that states what the outcome of the law vote was.
Fixed an issue where Renegades would sneak through undetected with Crackdown law active (Gurus and Project Phoenix).
Fixed an issue where the Economic Interventions law did not increase the least-stored advanced resource's production.
Fixed an issue where the Workers Shifts law could provide a higher than intended bonus.
Fixed an issue with the Tourist Campaign and Applicant Campaign laws so they can provide the exact promised amount of Applicants.
Fixed an issue with how the Seniors: Put Them to Work law interacts with the Forever Young breakthrough. Seniors who die during work no longer cause sanity loss in the colonists.
The Open Domes law is now preparable even if there is no Breathable Atmosphere.
The Open Domes law is no longer repealable. The Domes will only close if the Atmosphere becomes unbreathable.
Fixed an issue where the Open Floor action or Governing Assembly might suggest or enact laws that are not available.
The Founder’s Privilege law now correctly gets repealed when all Founders die or leave.
Fixed an issue where in some cases Faction Disasters would constantly start and stop.
Fixed some issues that could cause an onslaught of Faction Disasters from the same Faction.
Faction Disasters now stop when a Faction is Content or Happy.
Fixed an issue where Underground Domes appeared as empty while being populated.
Fixed an issue where Colonists could get stuck in Passages, making it impossible to salvage them.
Terraforming Special Projects no longer appear when Terraforming is maxed out.
Fixed an issue where some Techs would appear to be at >100% research progress.
Mars Reservation is no longer re-fabable.
The Last War mystery effects no longer stops Asteroid Landers from travelling to/from Asteroids.
Balance changes
Politics
Rebalanced the Assembly choice results.
Added Upkeep to some multiple choice laws (Applicant Campaign, Worker Shift Optimizations, Resource Subsidies, Crowded Living, Research Safety Standards).
Reduced the number of required researched Techs for Colony Independence Goal to 80 (was previously 120). This change applies only to new games.
Changed the number of Permits & Efficiency laws that The Dominion of Mars wants enacted, as in the early game it was very easy to go into a political crisis spiral.
Added new Faction likes / dislikes to make Dominion, GNow, Free Love and Martian First more agreeable and Utopia less agreeable.
Interplanetary Codex tasks for Ministries will no longer appear early in the game.
Launching High-speed Comms Satellite and SETI Satellite projects now require less Electronics.
UI
Fixed an issue where buildings under construction were very hard to select.
Fixed an issue where a Dust Storm notification wouldn’t despawn.
Fixed an issue where in some cases the arrow keys would navigate the HUD instead of scrolling.
“No sector set for scanning” warning no longer appears after all sectors have been scanned.
Added clarification that the Melting the Polar Caps mission will definitely cause a Dust Storm regardless of the Terraforming progress.
Added clarification that the Import Greenhouse Gases mission will definitely cause a Toxic Rain regardless of the Terraforming progress.
Added missing maintenance cost and remaining time to completion for the Earth Embassy.
Fixed an issue where an Earthsick notification could appear for recently dead Colonists.
Fixed an issue where a tooltip indicated that the Party Animal trait was recovering Health, rather than Comfort as expected.
Fixed an issue where a "Dome at risk" notification would display even if no Dome was at risk.
Clarified text about Cold Waves’ effect on buildings.
Fixed an issue where some Planetary points of interest could become unselectable.
Buildings in the Command Center are no longer displayed with Colonists icons
Modding
Added IDs to the XDef controls of UI elements
Dust storm and cold wave are now separate smaller functions
Gamepad
The bottom menus buttons’ navigation is now consistent with the info bar (D-pad Left selects the map change buttons).
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45747899/00ca2145ef0162f8901e4b84dd30afad5db57217.jpg"]
Hello Commander,

This update is packed with fixes and quality-of-life improvements. We’ve tackled the most common crash, overhauled Asteroid Lander controls, added new political laws to shape your colony, and smoothed out dozens of issues across colonists, trains, underground systems, and more!
Crash: Fixed crash related to switching maps (This is the most common crash experienced by the players.)
Steam and Epic only: Achievements can now be unlocked in playthroughs with active mods.
Implemented Manual Mode and Automated Mode for Asteroid Lander control:
For each Asteroid Lander the player can choose manual or automated mode via a button in the Lander infopanel. The default setting is manual mode.
Manual Mode operates similarly to the Resupply UI - the player can select Colonists, resources, and prefabs to/from an Asteroid to Mars. Players must initiate the landing manually.

In Automated Mode the player can set threshold values per Lander for selected resources. The Lander will export or import them automatically. The Asteroid Lander will reserve a landing spot both on Mars and the Asteroid. The Asteroid Lander will take off and land automatically.

Evacuation: A popup window now informs the player when an Asteroid is several hours from leaving. This popup window has a button to take the player to the Asteroid so they can load their landers and evacuate. Landers orbiting the Asteroid will automatically return to Mars.
Please be aware that Landers in existing savegames may not behave properly in some cases. Try requesting the payload again.
Fix for issue causing drones to continuously move resources between two Landers on the same Asteroid
Balance changes to water production and usage on asteroids
Tweaks to Asteroid maps generation to produce less clutter and provide more landing spots in some cases.
Implemented the Flatten tool on Asteroids to allow players to make the most of the limited space on asteroids.
Marsquakes no longer happen on Asteroids. Savegame fixup removes Marsquake rocks from Asteroids.
Fix for issue where the "Asteroid Arrived" notification would only appear if the asteroid was captured.
Pins with Landers that are ready to launch will now blink (similar to rockets).
Politics
Added 7 new laws that provide additional options to customize your colony:
“Energy focus” - a multi-choice law that will give a select type of power producers extra oomph but will reduce the performance of some of the other power producers.
“Terraforming focus” - a multi-choice law that will double the building bonuses for one terraforming parameter.
“Economic Interventions” - a law that will boost the production of the resource you have the least of, but has a high upkeep.
“Administration” - a multi-choice law that will allow you to reduce the upkeep of laws in funding or RP.
“Founder Privilege” - a law that gives extra Comfort to Founders when servicing their needs.
“Underground Amenities” - a law that gives underground Domes extra comfort
“Tourist Campaign” - a one-time law that adds a number of Tourist applicants when enacted.
Added new faction tasks and opportunities.
Added new Game Rule: “Political Freedom” - all laws are unlocked and players can directly Prepare and Vote on them.
Ministries are now single-shift buildings.
Rebalanced Ministries to give fixed bonuses to Laws. This alleviates some issues with fluctuating housing and workslots, as well as some imbalances in production.
"Drone Hub Efficiency" law now has an upkeep cost.
Faction Opportunities will not be generated if they have already timed out twice.
Changes and fixes to some faction likes and tasks.

notes.title: Laws changes that will apply to existing savegames

items.text: “Crowded Living” bonus is decreased and is now a fixed amount (3) instead of a percentage.
“Applicant Campaign” will provide a one-time applicant boost.
“Worker Shift Optimization” will have effect only if there is at least 1 worker in the shift.
Laws changes that won't apply to existing savegames but will be present in new games:
“Worker Shift Optimization” will use bonus values based on the number of shifts.
“Safety Standards Deregulation” will double the required maintenance resources for research buildings.
The “Productivity” option in the “Comfort” law will have a decreased bonus for worker performance.
“Resource Subsidies” will greatly increase rocket travel time.
Some law choices are now locked behind requirements. Affected laws are “Apportionment of Seats”, “Sensor Tower Usage”, and “Renegades”.
Diplomacy laws now require Earth Embassy.
Multiple choice laws are now repealable/revokeable.
Rebalanced "Independence" goal #2 to require enacting 30 laws (was 15).
Rebalanced "Independence" goal #4 to require 100 colonists with a comfort level of 70 (was 150).
Reordered independence techs and increased their required RP.
Added “Law upkeep” row to the Research UI.
Clarified descriptions of the Media Center and the Detainment Center that their effects apply only to the dome they are built in.
Underground
In new games the Underground entrances will appear in locations where they can be accessed from all directions. This will not affect existing savegames.
Marsquakes now correctly occur only in the Underground.
Removed Drones and Rovers from the Elevator UI.

Fixed an issue where the Bottomless Pit Lab could be rotated and freely placed in orientations that should not have been possible. Existing constructions and completed Labs will have to be cancelled or destroyed and placed anew. Stuck drones will not be affected by this fix.
Trains
Fixed an issue where stations connected via train tunnels would not transfer power.
Fixed tunnel power grids splitting incorrectly when deleting cables.
Increased the train station areas to service more workplaces/domes/habitats.
Trains will no longer attempt to traverse salvaged tunnels.
Trains can now be assigned to tracks by clicking on an object connected to the station (such as a tunnel).
Fixed an issue where track elements would remain on the map after the track they belonged to has been deleted.
Fixed multiple issues causing stations to not connect to tracks.
Fix for passenger trains not leaving stations.
Colonists

Fixes for cases of homeless/unemployed colonists, by updating how colonists evaluate domes for emigration, taking into account dome air/water/electricity supply, free residences, and vacant workplaces, preferring ones with matching specialization.
Fixed some cases of colonists walking back home and dying, instead of using trains.
Fixed an issue where colonists would overpopulate Habitats and die outside.
Fixed an issue where Tourists assigned to Naturalist and Micro-G Habitats would not live in them, exit and suffocate outside.
Rockets
Fixed an issue where Rockets would disappear when travelling to Earth.
Fixed an issue with missing Tourist overview in the Rocket infopanel and Notification.
Balance
Boosted yield of seed crops.
Fix for RC Dozer to load only Waste Rock.

Tweaks to building placement under pipes and tracks. Life support objects and objects serviced by shuttles can’t be placed under pipes because that leads to clipping and other problems. Players can’t construct tracks over existing buildings.
UI
Added option to disable edge scrolling.
Pre-game choices (such as Mission Sponsor, Commander Profile, selected Mystery, etc.) will be remembered between games.
Decreased the "Heavy Drone workload" notifications spam.
Fixed “Deposit running low” notification to appear only once per deposit.
Fixed “Hints Enabled” setting to properly set ‘on’/’off’/’once’ setting. This is now propagated to the Game Options menu as well.
Fixed contradicting Cold Wave countdown timers.
Controller: Selecting a pin with a gamepad won't move the camera to the pinned object.
General fixes
Fixed a bug where stockpiles were blocking tunnel construction.
Fixed the issue with Disasters (not starting/not ending/spamming notifications)
Fixed a case in which a Terraforming building may not update its working status.
Fix for issue where open air buildings like Ranches would reach 99% construction progress and not finish.
